places.name: Setúbal
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum, on the rise above the river. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.

The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 32% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; 2 stretches of the old wall inside were pulled down for a street along their line.
A great fire burned 6 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The duke planted a “New Town” across the river: one straight street of equal plots. It never prospered on its own, and the council bought it out a generation later.
A great fire burned 16 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 74% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; 2 stretches of the old wall inside were pulled down for a street along their line.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 75 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A great fire burned 23 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The old tower keep was rebuilt as a great castle on the same ground.
The parish church was pulled down and rebuilt on its own ground as a great minster.
A great fire burned 16 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Foz de Alva
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.

The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 80% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; 2 stretches of the old wall inside were pulled down for a street along their line; 1 houses were built into what was left of it.
A great fire burned 23 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
A great fire burned 9 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
A great fire burned 8 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Vauveiga
past: The old village of Vaelheim: farms about a green, with a little church, beside the road.
A hamlet grew up at the ford where the road crosses the river; a bridge replaced the ford in its second age. The old village kept its own church, outside the town’s bounds.
The ford was bridged in stone.
The duke planted a “New Town” across the river: one straight street of equal plots. It never prospered on its own, and the council bought it out a generation later.
3 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
Walled, the river and the lie of the land sparing a stretch of the circuit.
A great fire burned 17 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Casal de Moura
past: An older settlement grew into a town in Roman times. Its main routes survive, with irregular medieval lanes and plots shaped by the ground.
Walled.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 21 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the western side; 12 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
A great fire burned 22 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Alcáçova de Covas
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum, on the rise above the river. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 94% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line.
The Dominicans were given ground by the wall for their friary.
The keep was enlarged into a castle of stone.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 8 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A great fire burned 27 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
